report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The original 2024 AI Act text set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III, but this date has since been changed by the "AI Omnibus" amendment (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), which entered into force on 27 July 2026 ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727); [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Under current law, Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from **2 December 2027**, with a separate date of 2 August 2028 for high-risk AI embedded in regulated products under Annex I (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (Pre-Omnibus)
Under the original 2024 text of the AI Act, Annex III high-risk system obligations were to apply from 2 August 2026, 24 months after the Act's entry into force (medium confidence) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113); [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). The AI Act itself entered into force on 1 August 2024, with prohibited practices and AI literacy obligations applying from 2 February 2025 and governance/GPAI obligations from 2 August 2025 (low confidence) ([CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20); [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)). Notably, the European Parliament's general overview describes a 36-month timeline (implying ~August 2027) rather than 24 months, creating an unresolved inconsistency with other sources describing the pre-Omnibus baseline (medium confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The Commission adopted the AI Omnibus (Digital Package on Simplification) on 19 November 2025, proposing to delay high-risk rules by up to 16 months so that application would begin once the Commission confirmed that necessary standards and compliance tools were available (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai); [Consilium press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). Political agreement was reached on 7 May 2026, and the amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Current Applicable Dates
Following the Omnibus, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727); [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111); [Digital Strategy FAQ](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). Separately, obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products listed in Annex I now apply from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). A grandfathering provision under the amended Article 113/111 framework means that high-risk systems already placed on the market or put into service before the application date of Chapter III only become subject to the Regulation if they undergo significant design changes after that date (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727); [AI Act Service Desk, Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Multiple commercial and legal-analysis sources still cite 2 August 2026 as the operative Annex III deadline, apparently not reflecting the Omnibus amendment; this likely stems from outdated content predating the 27 July 2026 entry into force ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). The European Parliament's "36 months" framing conflicts with other sources' "24 months"/2 August 2026 description of the original timeline, and this discrepancy is unresolved in the available sources (medium confidence claims in tension). One low-confidence source (0.12) frames the Omnibus as a confirmed binding change ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)), while another low-confidence source treats the later dates as contingent "backstop" proposals that might not have been enacted before August 2026 ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO))—this is superseded by confirmation that the Omnibus did enter into force on 27 July 2026. A claim regarding Annex III conformity assessment requirements (Articles 8-15) carries low confidence (0.12) from a single, less-authoritative source ([AI Act Readiness guide](https://ai-act-readiness.example/annex-iii-obligations-guide)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether further delays are possible if harmonised standards are not finalized by December 2027, given the Omnibus's original conditional design tying application to standards availability. The precise scope of the Article 111/113 grandfather clause—specifically what qualifies as "significant changes in design"—is not fully detailed in available sources. It is also unclear whether 2 December 2027 applies uniformly across all Chapter III provisions or whether specific sub-provisions retain distinct dates.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The original 2024 AI Act text set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III, but this date has since been changed by the "AI Omnibus" amendment (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), which entered into force on 27 July 2026 ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727); [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Under current law, Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from **2 December 2027**, with a separate date of 2 August 2028 for high-risk AI embedded in regulated products under Annex I (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (Pre-Omnibus)
Under the original 2024 text of the AI Act, Annex III high-risk system obligations were to apply from 2 August 2026, 24 months after the Act's entry into force (medium confidence) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113); [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). The AI Act itself entered into force on 1 August 2024, with prohibited practices and AI literacy obligations applying from 2 February 2025 and governance/GPAI obligations from 2 August 2025 (low confidence) ([CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20); [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)). Notably, the European Parliament's general overview describes a 36-month timeline (implying ~August 2027) rather than 24 months, creating an unresolved inconsistency with other sources describing the pre-Omnibus baseline (medium confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The Commission adopted the AI Omnibus (Digital Package on Simplification) on 19 November 2025, proposing to delay high-risk rules by up to 16 months so that application would begin once the Commission confirmed that necessary standards and compliance tools were available (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai); [Consilium press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). Political agreement was reached on 7 May 2026, and the amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Current Applicable Dates
Following the Omnibus, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727); [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111); [Digital Strategy FAQ](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). Separately, obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products listed in Annex I now apply from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). A grandfathering provision under the amended Article 113/111 framework means that high-risk systems already placed on the market or put into service before the application date of Chapter III only become subject to the Regulation if they undergo significant design changes after that date (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727); [AI Act Service Desk, Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Multiple commercial and legal-analysis sources still cite 2 August 2026 as the operative Annex III deadline, apparently not reflecting the Omnibus amendment; this likely stems from outdated content predating the 27 July 2026 entry into force ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). The European Parliament's "36 months" framing conflicts with other sources' "24 months"/2 August 2026 description of the original timeline, and this discrepancy is unresolved in the available sources (medium confidence claims in tension). One low-confidence source (0.12) frames the Omnibus as a confirmed binding change ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)), while another low-confidence source treats the later dates as contingent "backstop" proposals that might not have been enacted before August 2026 ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO))—this is superseded by confirmation that the Omnibus did enter into force on 27 July 2026. A claim regarding Annex III conformity assessment requirements (Articles 8-15) carries low confidence (0.12) from a single, less-authoritative source ([AI Act Readiness guide](https://ai-act-readiness.example/annex-iii-obligations-guide)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether further delays are possible if harmonised standards are not finalized by December 2027, given the Omnibus's original conditional design tying application to standards availability. The precise scope of the Article 111/113 grandfather clause—specifically what qualifies as "significant changes in design"—is not fully detailed in available sources. It is also unclear whether 2 December 2027 applies uniformly across all Chapter III provisions or whether specific sub-provisions retain distinct dates.
